correctness.rationale: For any noncontracting real Hilbert embedding of wheel K1∨C_{2m}, m even-parity rim vectors have hub squared norm ≤T and mutual squared distances ≥4. The exact centroid identity mΣ||x_i||²−||Σx_i||²=Σ_{i<j}||x_i−x_j||² yields T≥2−2/m; equality forces each parity class to be a regular m-simplex of side 2 centered at the hub. Explicit 2m×2m rational Gram G with same-parity H=2I−2J/m and cross C=(1+1/m)(I+S^-1)−(S+S^-2)/m−2J/m is positive semidefinite: nonzero Fourier eigenvalues 2±2u[1+4(1−u²)/m], u=|cos(pi k/m)|; for m≥8 monotonicity bounds by 2, and m=7 uses a separate strict cosine rational bound. Rank=2m−2, and every graph pair is within squared factors [1,T] of its original shortest-path squared distance. This realizes exact c2=sqrt(2−2/m) for m≥7, including equality rigidity for all embeddings. Independent reconstructed numerical Gram spectra and all pairs for m=7,8,9,12,20,30,50 satisfy constraints; numerical tests are supplementary to Fourier positivity proof.
residual_risks: The separate m=7 cosine estimate is essential; the monotonic derivative argument is alone valid only m≥8.
Numerical Gram eigenvalues are not an exact certificate for every m, but the Fourier eigenvalue bound is analytical.
